findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss exceptions
findings.body: The reader thread is started but never joined. Right after `deletedAll.set(true)`, the test calls `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` while the reader may still be inside a `groups(...)` request that overlaps the last deletions. An exception from that request is added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed. The thread can also outlive the test and keep calling the admin client during cleanup or the next test. Keep a reference to the thread, `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting, and consider asserting that at least one read actually ran.

findings.title: Same NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three paginated `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. When the group is deleted concurrently, the delegate lookup returns null and these methods throw a NullPointerException. These methods back the sub-group listing endpoints, so concurrent reads plus deletes can still produce 500s. Apply the same null handling, for example return `Stream.empty()`.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body: The 100 created groups are only removed by the test's own deletion loop. If group creation or deletion fails partway through, the remaining groups are left in the shared managed realm. They can then break other tests, for example name-conflict or group-count assertions. Register each created id with `managedRealm.cleanup()`, or delete them in a finally block.
